text:
maya: Thinking about short 10-30s surges where an org bursts but steady-state is low. Current token-bucket + org-reservoir is flagging a lot of false SLA hits. Anyone up for discussing a "grace crediting" approach that decays faster for short spikes?

frank: I like the idea. Do you mean a separate short-window bucket that gives extra headroom, then ages out quickly?

maya: Exactly. Two-tier: long-term bucket for sustained throughput, and ephemeral credits for micro-surges. Ephemeral credits have TTL and a steep decay curve so they don't permanently increase quota.

ops-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for feature/ephemeral-crediting (5% traffic) :rocket:

sarah: curious about fairness: how do we prevent a noisy tenant from exhausting ephemeral credits repeatedly and hurting others? need cross-org smoothing.

maya: proposal: ephemeral credits are bounded per-org and charged against a global short-window reservoir with per-priority weights. If X org consumes >Y% of reservoir in window, throttle its ephemeral rate with backoff factor.

ali: sounds right. also we should keep per-key metrics so product teams can debug: ephemeral_used, ephemeral_left, reservoir_used. Add PromQL for alerts.

jordan: small nit: need jitter on refill timers or we'll get coordinated refills and synchronized spikes. add +/- 10% jitter on refill interval.

frank: agreed. also let's avoid a hard cutoff switch between buckets. do a smoothing transfer: when long-term bucket low, borrow from ephemeral with an increasing penalty to score so cost shows on console.

maya: example config sketch:
```
short_window: 30s
short_bucket_size: 500 tokens
short_refill: 250 tokens / 30s (jitter 10%)
short_ttl: 120s
long_bucket_size: 10000 tokens
long_refill: 1000 tokens / 60s
borrow_penalty: 1.5 (multiplier for billing/score)
global_reservoir: 20000 tokens
```

sarah: thanks — for telemetry, here's a starter PromQL to track short-window exhaustion across orgs: 
```
sum by (org) (rate(short_bucket_consumed_tokens[30s])) / sum(rate(short_bucket_capacity[30s])) > 0.8
```

ali: can we show an estimated "minutes of headroom" in console per org and per-key? UX should show ephemeral vs long-term split and a clear history spike chart. product teams need that to tune prompts.

maya: yes. console should surface: current_ephemeral_left, projected_depletion_at_current_rate, recent_bump_events (list). Also checkbox to opt-out of ephemeral borrowing (for orgs who prefer strict steady-state caps).

frank: rollout plan: dogfood in prod teams for 48h, then canary to 10% for 24h with synthetic spike generator hitting various org weights. Monitor three metrics: P99 latency, ephemeral_borrow_rate, cross-org_reservoir_share.

ops-bot: incident: synthetic-surge-test reported spike in org "alpha-corp" — ephemeral borrowed 95% of global_reservoir, auto-throttled at 1991234578 :warning:

jordan: that incident showed a bug: borrow_penalty wasn't applied in billing pipeline so cost visibility was wrong. I pushed a small fix to feature branch.

maya: good catch. action items: (1) add jitter and TTL enforcement (jordan), (2) wire borrow_penalty to billing and console (frank + ali), (3) expand telemetry queries and alerts (sarah), (4) schedule prod dogfood run and synthetic tests (maya).

ali: I'll mock console panel and expose an API endpoint /orgs/{id}/credits that returns ephemeral & long buckets + projected depletion. JSON sample in the RFC will be shared.

sarah: can we add a regression alert if an org's ephemeral borrow rate increases >3x baseline in 15m? that would catch sudden bad actors.

frank: yes, add alert and an auto-fallback policy: when triggered, reduce ephemeral refill to 25% for that org for 5m and notify the org owner slack handle.

maya: one more UX thought: show "reason" tags on throttles (steady-state cap vs ephemeral exhaustion vs global-reservoir-throttle) so SREs and customers know what happened.

ops-bot: deploy: feature/ephemeral-crediting bumped to 10% canary at 1991234590 :white_check_mark:

jordan: I'll follow up PR for billing patch and a test that covers borrow flows.

maya: thanks everyone — will post the RFC doc link here after I clean up the config + telemetry sections. :heart:
